verdict: APPROVE — the set finally schedules its openings and every claim on paper is member-true: census exact on all three scenes (15/5/40, marks D1…/W1… deterministic), RO/header cells verbatim (16-ft door prints 'ENGINEERED (by supplier)', CMU openings 'precast lintel'), composed red flags print WHOLE under their rows (zero ellipsis anywhere), pagination splits on row-groups with (p/N) titles, cover indexes the sheet and SHEET n/N stays contiguous through 15/9/10-sheet sets, and the blast radius is surgically clean — pin-without-walls is byte-EQUAL to master on all 14 demo sheets, and with walls only cover (+index row), wall plan (+bubbles/legend) and the new sheet differ, so electrical/MEP/takeoff regression holds by construction. Two FLAG-class composition items ride the board, not the merge: (1) the bubble registry sees GLYPHS only — D2/D3 in the pilot exhibit park exactly ON the A-A cut line (white knockout keeps them legible; the pilot's flagged case confirmed as cosmetic) and 3 of the demo's 15 bubbles (W3, D1, W5) land on T-junction/corner wall linework; (2) the P1 sparseness call — judged: FOLD small schedules into the Schedules sheet (the pilot's pre-accepted fallback) when the whole table+flags fits ~1/3 page (the 5-opening sheet is ~80% empty and does scream half-empty); the demo's 15-row sheet is acceptable dedicated.

RO/header cells are member-verbatim (gated byte-match; spot-checked D1 4x8, W5 4x10, D3/D5/D6 4x6, 9 CMU openings 'precast lintel'). Four red ⚑ flags print WHOLE under their rows, word-wrapped, indented — incl. the two-line composed 'ENGINEERED BEAM REQUIRED — … | header 4x12 does not fit … (9.4" of 11.3") — raise the wall, lower the opening, or use an engineered flat header' on the pilot's D2. Ellipsis scan across every schedule SVG: zero hits. Stress 1/2 holds W1-W39 with the last row 120px above the title block; 2/2 holds W40; every mark exactly once (gated + counted on paper).
FOCUS-1-schedule-table-legibility.note: Doors print '—' in SILL AFF; sill heights for windows come from the OpeningSlice (2'-11.44" etc.) and read cleanly. Wall column prints raw host ids (wall_x86jgwle7bdzjmis) — machine-y but unambiguous and the cross-reference is honest; friendlier wall tags would need a naming scheme the model doesn't have.

FOCUS-2-wall-plan-mark-bubbles.evidence: Every schedule row's mark is findable on its wall plan: 15/15 (demo), 5/5 (pilot), 40/40 (stress); bubbles pairwise ≥15px and ≥15px from the A-A END bubbles (gated + verified); no crowded-fallback comment fired on any scene; each bubble sits adjacent to its own opening (D3's directly under its flagged header, D2 beside its RO and clear of the A-A dashed line on the demo). THE FLAG — the registry sees glyphs, not ink: (a) the pilot's D2/D3 case (both openings at plan x=4 where sectionCutX lands): both bubbles park exactly ON the A-A cut line — centers on the line, white fill knocking it out (crop-p5-d2/d3.png). Legible and unambiguous (r=8 'D2' text vs the r=10 'A' marks), but the cut line now visually dead-ends into a door mark on both walls — a drafting-convention wobble, not a lie. (b) demo W3/D1/W5: the perpendicular ±14px offset from the OWNING wall lands on a CROSSING wall at T-junctions/corners — three bubbles' white fill occludes ~16px of stem-wall/corner framing linework (crop-w3d1.png, crop-w5.png). All three stay legible (white knockout + black rim is accepted mark practice) and 12 of 15 demo bubbles are fully clear.
FOCUS-2-wall-plan-mark-bubbles.note: Cheap board-queue fix, no new machinery: push sampled points of the section line (every ~20px) and the wall-band rects into placed[] (wallPlan data is already in scope) — the existing candidate walk (t-offsets exist but are never preferred) then slides D2/D3 off the line and the T-junction trio off the stems for free. ADVISORIES.evidence: (a) The demo W5 row prints the AGGREGATED per-(size,thickness)-class flag '2x4 framing compressed to 2.94" — 0.100m drawn wall holds…' because that class flag rides its header member — honest (the flag IS on the member) but it reads as if the compression were about that opening; consider stripping class-aggregate flags (the S7 'compressed' family) from schedule rows or prefixing 'wall:'. (b) The wall-sheet legend's single 'header — 4x6' row keys one size while the schedule proves three header sizes on the level (4x6/4x8/4x10) — pre-existing legend convention, byte-identical to master, but the new schedule now makes the mismatch visible; a 'headers per schedule' legend wording would reconcile them.
ADVISORIES.note: Neither is a B21d defect; both are follow-the-new-sheet polish.
